title: POC weekly: env access + security brief
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on environment access, security review, and interpreting early benchmark artifacts. Redwood reviewed temporary gateway setup, KV cache warmup behavior, and a plan for private deployment SSO/KMS handoff. Customer asked for SOC 2/arch docs and end-to-end benchmark runs with their traffic profile. Next: Redwood to send security packet and run 10k request benchmark with seeded dataset; customer to provide final SSO metadata and confirm service account permissions.
meeting_header: Recorded: 2026-03-05 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Raman, Marcus Chen (Redwood) — Alex Moore, Dana Ruiz, Samir Patel, Lina Park (BrightWave)
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Alright, hi everyone, thanks for joining. We'll kick off. This is the weekly POC check — quick status then security items and the benchmark run results. Priya, you wanna start with the perf highlights?
[00:22] Priya Raman: Yeah, sure. So we ran the 2k-query smoke yesterday against the staging gateway. Median for short prompts was around 95ms p50, p95 about 340ms, that includes network overhead. There was one spike at about 1.2s that looks like a cold kv cache miss — k v cache, excuse me — so warming helped.
[00:46] Dana Ruiz: When you say kv miss, is that because of the prefix cache not persisting between requests? Our traffic will be very bursty — long tails.
[01:05] Priya Raman: Right, so our default prefix caching keeps per-session KV for a rolling window, but in your config we suggested a longer ttl. For the pilot we've set the KV window to 120s which reduced the p95 to ~260ms in follow-up tests. But with the bigger 10k run we plan to tune batching thresholds.
[01:34] Alex Moore: Quick Q — is batching on by default for the hosted side? We worry about latency vs cost; for real-time UI we need <200ms 90% ideally.
[01:48] Marcus Chen: Batching is workload-aware — it only aggregates similar-length tokens up to your latency SLO. You can set a hard p90 cap and we'll prioritize latency and fall back to single-request paths. That will cost more but keep latency consistency.
[02:14] Samir Patel: On security — we looked at the readme but want to go deeper. SOC two type two status? And audits, logs retention? Also KMS/HSM integration — does Redwood support customer-managed KMS for private deployment?
[02:36] Jordan Lee: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated. For hosted we offer envelope encryption with Redwood KMS but you can bring-your-own for Private. We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO-27001 artifacts; I'll share the packet after the call.
[02:54] Samir Patel: Can you share specifics about token-level logs and redaction? We need to avoid PHI being stored unintentionally.
[03:09] Priya Raman: Good call. Logs are configurable by route; you can opt-out of request/response retention for sensitive routes. We also have automatic PII scrubbing heuristics, though you should treat those as supplemental — best practice is to filter client-side before sending.
[03:30] Lina Park: For the pilot we plan to send de-identified clinical notes but still need the audit trail. Is there an immutable audit that shows who accessed what model and when?
[03:44] Jordan Lee: Yes, audit logs are available with user identity (SSO/SAML) and service account ID, with timestamps and model/version used. These logs can be integrated into your SIEM; retention is configurable per contract.
[04:02] Dana Ruiz: Networking — we're leaning towards VPC peering for the Private deployment. Any gotchas for peering with GCP projects?
[04:15] Marcus Chen: We've done GCP and AWS. Key items: route advertisement, egress costs, and MTU sizing. Also, for peered VPCs you need to allow tcp/443 and the specific control-plane IP ranges we provide. We'll send the exact CIDR list.
[04:35] Alex Moore: What about HSM-backed key operations? Our compliance team insists on HSM for key lifecycle.
[04:44] Jordan Lee: HSM integrations are available for Private deployments; we support HSM-backed KMS through partner integrations. For Dedicated we can negotiate HSM attachments as part of the contract.
[04:58] [00:05:00] Priya Raman: Back to perf, we did a short quantization pass on the model variant which reduced memory by ~30% and cut median latency by ~10% for longer sequences. There's a small quality delta; we've logged a couple of hallucination regressions on named-entity prompts in the eval harness.
[05:25] Samir Patel: Are those regressions visible in the eval dashboard? We need to be able to tie regressions to a prompt set and roll back.
[05:36] Priya Raman: Yes, Redwood Optimize ties regressions to prompt sets and you can auto-fallback to an earlier variant. We'll demonstrate the rollback playground in the next technical deep-dive.
[05:50] Alex Moore: Ok, about access — Dana has been trying to get the service account and SSO metadata to you. Dana?
[05:58] Dana Ruiz: Yeah, I shared a SAML metadata file but I think some attributes were missing — we didn't include the NameID format that your SSO connector expects. I'll re-export and include group mappings.
[06:12] Jordan Lee: Great. Make sure to include the certificate and the ACS url exactly as in the doc. We'll validate and return a test assertion.
[06:20] [00:10:00] Lina Park: On the benchmarks, can you run a 10k request run that mirrors our client-side batching? We want to test end-to-end latency under the bursty pattern.
[06:31] Priya Raman: Absolutely. Our plan is to run three 10k sweeps: one with small prompts, one with mixed lengths, and one with your real traffic trace if you hand it over (sanitized). We will share raw traces and aggregated p50/p90/p95/p99.
[06:49] Samir Patel: For the legal side, can you confirm data residency? We need EU CC's to keep data in eu-west.
[06:58] Jordan Lee: Hosted tenancy can be region-locked to eu-west for data residency. For Private it's naturally in your network. We'll include the options in the security packet.
[07:10] [00:15:00] Marcus Chen: A note on the gateway — we saw TLS renegotiation issues when the concurrency spiked; we recommended enabling connection pooling on your side for the pilot. That reduced the overhead by about 40ms average.
[07:29] Dana Ruiz: Ok we'll flip pooling on in staging and rerun.
[07:34] Priya Raman: Also, regarding fallback strategies: we can configure automatic fallback to a smaller model family if your primary runs out of capacity, or route to a different region. The most important is to set a sensible ranking rule so quality vs cost tradeoffs are explicit.
[07:53] Alex Moore: We're exploring a hybrid approach — hosted for early dev, dedicated for production. What's the timeline to move to dedicated?
[08:02] Jordan Lee: Typically 6–8 weeks after signature for capacity provisioning, can be faster with committed sizing. We'll draft capacity profiles to match your expected peak qps.
[08:14] [00:20:00] Samir Patel: Legal question — retention windows for logs if we opt into extended retention? Cost and access controls?
[08:24] Jordan Lee: Extended retention is an add-on. You can specify role-based access and have read-only export credentials for the SIEM. We'll include pricing tiers in the packet.
[08:36] Lina Park: For the next check-in I'd like to see the 10k run results and the security packet. Also, a short demo of the rollback playground.
[08:48] Priya Raman: We'll aim to share the 10k results within 72 hours and the security packet today.
[08:55] [00:25:00] Dana Ruiz: Quick potential blocker — our infra team needs the service account to be able to create route and DNS entries. Can we scope down the permissions to just what you need?
[09:05] Marcus Chen: Yes, least-privilege is supported. For the initial staging we need 'compute.networkAdmin' equivalent and create cloud-dns records; for production we'll move to narrower roles. We'll supply a permissions manifest.
[09:20] Samir Patel: On redaction, is there a way to run a pre-send hook inside our VPC that scrubs data before it's proxied to Redwood?
[09:31] Jordan Lee: For Private deployments you can run a sidecar or ingress filter. For hosted, we recommend client-side SDK hooks. We can share example middleware.
[09:43] [00:30:00] Alex Moore: Any thoughts about competing vendors? We did a short eval vs OpenAI and noticed cost differences for embeddings and token pricing.
[09:54] Jordan Lee: Price comparisons vary by workload; Redwood's differentiator is the ability to tune batching, cache and quantization to lower per-token costs while keeping latency SLOs. We'll share a cost model spreadsheet.
[10:06] Priya Raman: And for the regression noted earlier, we'll include the exact prompt that triggered the change and a diff of logits; I noted that the regression was on named entity resolution in the clinical domain, so your eval team can review.
[10:20] Dana Ruiz: Great.
[10:22] [00:35:00] Jordan Lee: Recap — Redwood deliverables: 1) security packet (SOC 2/ISO/KMS/HSM options) today, 2) permissions manifest for the service account and CIDR list for peering, 3) three 10k benchmark sweeps with raw traces and aggregate metrics within 72h, 4) demo of rollback playground in next tech deep-dive. BrightWave deliverables: SAML metadata with NameID and group mappings, sanitized traffic trace for the mixed-length 10k run, confirmation on VPC peering CIDR.
[10:52] Samir Patel: We'll prioritize the SAML and traffic trace this week.
[10:57] Jordan Lee: Cool. Anything else before we close?
[11:00] Lina Park: Nope, thanks.
[11:02] Jordan Lee: Thanks all — we'll follow up in email with the packet and invite for the next technical deep-dive.
[11:10] [00:45:00] (meeting ends)

Priya Raman: Run three 10k benchmark sweeps (small, mixed, sanitized real trace) and upload raw traces + aggregate report — due 2026-03-08
Marcus Chen: Provide permissions manifest and control-plane CIDR list for VPC peering — due 2026-03-06
Dana Ruiz: Re-export SAML metadata with NameID format and group mappings; share sanitized traffic trace — due 2026-03-06
